objective: Transform labeled synthetic OPTASK-style raw messages into source-traceable frequency plans, crypto change-over windows and flight quarters on a reviewable consolidated 24-hour UTC schedule.

invocation.input: Object with exactly documents: array of {documentId:string,rawText:string}, selectedDay:string; optional shipId:string|null (default null), decisions:array of {documentId:string,eventId:string,decision:string} (default []). All fields and validation precedence are specified in rules. No model environment is required.
invocation.output: Object with exactly status:"ok"|"review"|"error", error:null|string, disclosure:string, events:array, reviewItems:array, headers:array. Event, span, diagnostic and header structures, ordering, error vocabulary and status derivation are specified in rules. No extra response fields.
rules: Only the object input described here is supported; there is no action discriminator. Unknown object keys are rejected at every request level. Envelope checks occur before parsing. Validation precedence: INVALID_REQUEST for shape/type/unknown keys/limits, then EMPTY_INPUT for documents.length=0 or any rawText consisting only of whitespace, then INVALID_DAY, INVALID_SHIP, INVALID_DECISIONS. Return the error envelope with no partial results. Optional fields omitted use defaults; null is invalid everywhere except shipId, which means no filter. IDs match ^[A-Z0-9-]+$; shipId uses the same grammar. selectedDay is a real Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD in years 1900..9999. No implicit clock dates.

Accept 0..32 documents, each rawText at most 500000 UTF-16 units; documentId nonempty at most 80 characters. decisions defaults to []; shipId defaults to null. Decision shape is {documentId:string,eventId:string,decision:"include"|"exclude"}. References must resolve to exactly one parsed candidate and each pair may occur only once, else INVALID_DECISIONS. A duplicate local event ID in one document is not eligible for decisions. Selected day is explicit; header DAY is source metadata and need not equal it. All display is UTC (Z).

The exact invented grammar is documented in data/README.md and repeated here. Four headers in order: SYNTHETIC / NOT VALIDATED AGAINST REAL USMTF ; MSGID/OPTASK/<id>/REV=<positive integer>// ; UNIT/<id>// ; DAY/<valid date>/ZONE=Z//. Each occupies one line; ENDMSG// must be the last nonempty line. Accept LF and CRLF mixed; optional final newline, ignore empty body lines. Header/terminator defects produce one INVALID_HEADER diagnostic at the first offending line and no candidates for that document. Empty source is an envelope EMPTY_INPUT. REMARK/ through // is inert prose including extra slashes, Unicode or apparent instructions; never extract from it. All other unsupported body lines yield UNSUPPORTED_LINE.

Body records in exact key order: FREQPLAN/ID=<id>/PLAN=<nonempty>/NET=<nonempty>/MHZ=<decimal>/UNIT=MHz/START=<timestamp>/END=<timestamp>// ; CRYPTO/ID=<id>/REF=<nonempty>/START=<timestamp>/END=<timestamp>// ; FLIGHTQ/ID=<id>/CONTEXT=<nonempty>/START=<timestamp>[/END=<timestamp>]//. No field value contains slash, CR or LF. Category/keys are case-sensitive, no padding. ID uses the ID grammar. Decimal MHZ matches digits with optional dot and digits and must be finite >0. Other category structural defects are MALFORMED_RECORD. Missing END for FREQPLAN/CRYPTO is MISSING_END (before generic structural error). Duplicated local ID: emit DUPLICATE_ID on every occurrence and suppress all candidates with that ID.

Timestamps strictly match YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm±HH:mm, years 1900..9999, real Gregorian dates, hours 00..23, minutes 00..59, offsets at most 14:00. No seconds or DST inference. A syntactically zone-free YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm gives MISSING_ZONE; all other invalid timestamps give INVALID_DATE. END must be strictly later than START; equality or earlier yields END_BEFORE_START. No rollover or header-zone fallback. One diagnostic per invalid event line with precedence DUPLICATE_ID, MISSING_END, MALFORMED_RECORD, INVALID_FREQUENCY, START timestamp error, END timestamp error, END_BEFORE_START. Invalid lines emit no event; valid siblings survive.

Output event shape exactly matches the documented intake event schema: eventId,documentId,category (FREQPLAN|CRYPTO|FLIGHTQ),messageId,shipId,revision (integer),originalFields (every event key exactly as raw strings),normalized {startUtc,endUtc,frequencyMHz},kind (interval|point),durationMinutes,selectedDay {startMinute,endMinute,visible,clippedStartMinute,clippedEndMinute},reviewStatus,source {line,range,fields}. UTC strings are YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ without milliseconds. Missing END means null endUtc only for FLIGHTQ point, duration 0. frequencyMHz numeric only for FREQPLAN, otherwise null. Spans are {start,end,text}, half-open UTF-16 indices into unchanged rawText; line is one-based; range excludes CR/LF. source.fields maps category and every originalFields key to its value span (category span is the category keyword). Derived values inherit original evidence, never invented literal spans.

Durations are elapsed minutes. Relative startMinute and endMinute are signed minutes from selected UTC midnight; points have equal values. Interval visible iff startMinute<1440 and endMinute>0. Point visible iff 0<=startMinute<1440. For visible entries clip start/end to [0,1440]; invisible entries have both clipped fields null. Keep out-of-day entries in events and do not merge overlaps. Filter events by exact shipId if supplied; headers and diagnostics retain all documents. Sort events by UTC start, documentId in Unicode code-unit order, then source.line. No category priorities or operational conflict doctrine.

Deduplicate equal documentId plus byte-for-byte equal decoded rawText, retaining the first. Different rawText under the same documentId suppresses all versions of that identity and emits DOCUMENT_ID_CONFLICT at line 1 for its first occurrence. Headers array follows first-document order, one per successfully parsed unique document: {documentId,fields}, fields maps messageId,shipId,revision,selectedDay,displayZone to spans. displayZone span points to the Z after ZONE=, not the first matching Z. Header identity spans refer to literal values. Header spans remain available regardless of ship filter.

Candidates sharing messageId,shipId,eventId across distinct documents with different revisions are revision alternatives. Preserve all and set reviewStatus=revision_review, with REVISION_REVIEW diagnostics on each event line until every alternative has a decision and exactly one is include. Never auto-supersede by revision number. Decisions apply before ship filtering; selected include becomes included and exclude becomes excluded (retain excluded events/evidence). Other candidates start unreviewed, becoming included/excluded only by decision. Incomplete or conflicting revision decisions leave all alternatives revision_review and all group diagnostics. No textual edits are accepted as decisions: corrected raw text must be reparsed with new spans and decisions reset by UI.

Diagnostic shape exactly {documentId,line,code,source}; line is one-based and source is a whole-line span excluding CR/LF. Codes are INVALID_HEADER,UNSUPPORTED_LINE,MISSING_END,MALFORMED_RECORD,DUPLICATE_ID,INVALID_FREQUENCY,MISSING_ZONE,INVALID_DATE,END_BEFORE_START,DOCUMENT_ID_CONFLICT,REVISION_REVIEW. Sort diagnostics by first-document order, line, then code lexicographically. For duplicate document identity conflicts use the first text only for diagnostic evidence. Headers omitted for invalid/conflicted documents. Error envelope is {status:"error",error:<envelope error code>,disclosure:<fixed disclosure>,events:[],reviewItems:[],headers:[]}. Success envelope has same six keys, error:null. status="review" if any diagnostic exists or any retained filtered event is unreviewed/revision_review, otherwise "ok". Valid zero-event messages yield ok, never human approval. No hidden state between invocations.

UI and host evaluator POST this exact JSON to /api/invoke and receive the raw computed envelope; application tests import the same backend compute entrypoint. No model explanation, OCR, remote API, operational transmission or actual crypto material exists. Disclosure is exactly: Synthetic, not validated against the real USMTF format. All exports include this disclosure, originals, normalized values, header/field evidence and explicit decisions. JSON export is a browser-created wrapper {disclosure,selectedDay,shipId,documents,decisions,result} of the current saved successful response and its exact request; it must not export stale drafts as reviewed.

capabilities.description: Extract all three mock OPTASK categories and exact evidence; abstain on malformed records and inert prose.
Normalize explicit zones, compute durations, ship filtering and half-open UTC-day clipping without changing instants.
Deduplicate identical documents, retain revision alternatives, apply explicit per-event decisions and expose review state.
